acceptance_criteria: differential replay reproduces the archived ledger state for every ticket; every uuid appears in exactly one file before and after; a dry run prints the evidence used for each adoption
task.description: One pass over the root ledger's 151 task_created events routed by scope.repo: 79 stay at root (gaugeblock 29, workspace 20, none 30); 52 move (outfeed 26, benchwork 17, storypole 7, chalkline 6, sawhorse 5, miter 4, joiner 2, rabbet 2, dado 1, batten 1). Adoption: all 30 unscoped tickets carry crate_name, so ownership is provable rather than guessed, giving 20 adoptions (benchwork 5, storypole 5, miter 4, sawhorse 2, outfeed joiner common 1 each) and 10 staying at root as cross-cutting (crate=workspace 8, plan-at-root 1, two-repo GB-45). common gains a CM prefix, a config and a store. Prefixes never route: GB-17 lives in benchwork with a GB- key under the keep-existing-keys decision, and the prefix map is consulted only when minting a new key. Movement is a file move, not a log edit; the pre-migration ledger is retained at ledger-archive/ledger-2026-11.jsonl.

HALF DONE 2026-11-08 (commit 4c8d152): the plan is implemented, the apply is not.

The routing is computed and inspectable before anything moves, with the evidence for every decision: scope
(the ticket's repo names a member), crate (adoption when exactly one repository owns the crate), suite (the
suite's own aliases), unclaimed (a repository no member claims), unscoped (no evidence at all).

Six tests. Two guard the rules most easily got wrong: a suite pseudo-crate is not an owner even when the lookup
offers one, and per_member() plus staying() must equal the ticket total, so the routing cannot silently drop a
ticket.

Still owed, and deliberately not half-built here:
  - apply: write the records, compact the root ledger, and assert the differential replay - the resulting
    records must replay to the same task states as the ledger they came from. That assertion is the only thing
    that makes a destructive migration safe, so it ships with the code it guards rather than being retrofitted;
  - the crate-to-repository map from the workspace topology, which the CLI will pass into plan();
  - a --dry-run verb so the real numbers come from the real ledger rather than from a test fixture.

The expected numbers, from the analysis recorded on SP-34: 151 task_created events, 79 staying at the root
(gaugeblock 29, workspace 20, none 30), 52 moving, and 20 of the 30 unscoped adopted by crate evidence.

apply writes records, verifies by differential replay, and archives the ledger last - in that order, so a failed
verification costs only deletable files while the original history still exists. The replay compares the fields a
reader would see rather than event bytes, and checks both directions: no task may change meaning, and no task may
go missing.

Three tests cover the happy path, an unroutable destination (ledger and archive untouched), and the replay's
reader-visible comparison.

     rather than a fixture.

DRY RUN 2026-11-08 against the real suite store, installed binary v0.1.0-beta.5:

  350 ticket(s); 159 stay at the root, 191 move, 72 adopted by crate evidence

The earlier estimate on this ticket said 151 -> 79 staying, 52 moving, 20 adopted. That was WRONG and the error was
mine: it counted task_created events only, and deferred items also carry a whole task. 151 created + 172 deferred
+ splits and later additions is the 350 the replay actually holds. So the migration is roughly 3.6 times larger
than described, and adoption is 72 tickets rather than 20.

That changes the risk profile rather than the mechanism: 191 tickets changing repository is a large working-tree
change, and 72 of them are adopted on crate evidence from tickets filed weeks ago, where the crate name may no
longer reflect where the work landed. The differential replay protects against losing or altering state; it does
not protect against routing a ticket to the wrong repository.

NOT RUN. The engine is tested and the dry run is real, but the numbers moved by a factor of 3.6 from what was
reviewed and approved. Running it now would be the same mistake this session opened with - changing durable
state on an assumption nobody re-read. The dry run output is the thing to review, and the plan should be
inspected per ticket (or narrowed, e.g. migrate only tickets created after a date) before it is applied.

BLOCKER FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE RUNNING 2026-11-08 (commit e23a6b3).

Checking where the migration would actually write turned up a defect that no dry run could show: common/ has
.gaugeblock/docs.toml and no storypole/ subdirectory, and seven scope-routed tickets point at it. resolve_dot_dir
fell through to .storypole in that case, so the migration would have created a legacy store inside a repository
that never had one - the same drift this migration exists to end, committed by the migration itself.

Fixed: legacy is used only when it exists. Two tests cover the common shape and a real legacy repository.

Two incidental fixes from the same change: store.rs crossed the line limit and its write path moved to
store/writes.rs, and the rollup duplicate-task message was nondeterministic because members come from a HashMap -
it now sorts its sources, so the same pair is always named in the same order.

The migration is now clear to run: 119 scope moves, evidence-backed, with the archive as the undo. Still not run -
that is a deliberate end-of-session decision, not a technical blocker.
